examples.text: Реакция положительная. Людям нравится.
examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'idea' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, буду рад видеть вас в ресторане.
examples.trans: Hello, I will be glad to see you in the restaurant.

examples.text: Это очень хорошо, нам нравится идея.
examples.trans: That is very good, we like the idea.

examples.text: Витя, ты не видел мою тунику?
examples.trans: Vitya, have you seen my tunic?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Подожди, нам твои деньги не нужны.
examples.trans: Wait, we do not need your money.

examples.text: Это твой кофе.
examples.trans: This is your coffee.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Отлично, я приеду за день до показа.
examples.trans: Excellent, I will arrive a day before the show.

examples.text: Модельер весь день за нами следит.
examples.trans: The designer watches us all day long.

examples.text: Подожди, нам твои деньги не нужны.
examples.trans: Wait, we do not need your money.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('needed').

examples.text: Нам нужно очень хорошо к нему подготовиться.
examples.trans: We need to prepare very well for it.

examples.text: Подожди, нам твои деньги не нужны.
examples.trans: Wait, we do not need your money.

examples.text: Нам с Полиной нужно холодное шампанское.
examples.trans: Polina and I need some cold champagne.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно, ребята, всем пока до завтра.
examples.trans: Alright, guys, bye everyone until tomorrow.

examples.text: Ладно, ребята, тогда мы с вами договорились.
examples.trans: Alright, guys, then we have a deal.

examples.text: Ладно, мы до завтра спокойно потерпим.
examples.trans: Alright, we will calmly be patient until tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А я главный шеф-повар этого ресторана.
examples.trans: And I am the head chef of this restaurant.

examples.text: Свежий зелёный салат для четвёртого столика.
examples.trans: Fresh green salad for the fourth table.

examples.text: Вот он скоро приедет, тогда скажу.
examples.trans: Once he arrives soon, then I will tell him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, я внимательно слушаю, Элеонора Андреевна.
examples.trans: Yes, I am listening attentively, Eleonora Andreyevna.

examples.text: Миша, скоро у нас модный показ.
examples.trans: Misha, soon we will have a fashion show.

examples.text: Нам нужно очень хорошо к нему подготовиться.
examples.trans: We need to prepare very well for it.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говориться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'agreed, deal', paired with 'договариваться'.

examples.text: Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы договорились.
examples.trans: We've agreed.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
